evidence.text:
Pd-Catalyzed Enantioselective Creation of All-Carbon Quaternary
Center with 2,3-Allenylic Carbonates
Jie Lin, Minqiang Jia, Xu Song, Hao Yu,* and Shengming Ma*
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2024, 26, 2349−2353
 Read Online
ACCESS
Metrics & More
 Article Recommendations *
sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: Enantioselective construction of all-carbon quaternary centers has been achieved via the palladium-catalyzed highly
enantioselective allenylation of oxindoles with 2,3-allenylic carbonates to afford a variety of optically active allene products, which
contain oxindole units with different functional groups, in high ee. The corresponding synthetic applications have also been
demonstrated.
T
he wide occurrence of the allene unit in natural products,
biologically active compounds, and marketed drugs,
1
as
well as the diversified reactivities,
2
have promoted the rapid
development of allene chemistry in the last three decades.
Recently, much effort has been devoted to the asymmetric
synthesis of allenes with a unique axial chirality.
3
One of the
most straightforward methods would be the metal-catalyzed
enantioselective allenylation of a nucleophile with racemic 2,3-
allenol derivatives constructing an axial chirality and/or center
chirality within the allene starting material (Scheme 1a, eq 1).
4−6
However, extensive studies on differently substituted 2,3-allenol
derivatives have been focused on the construction of a chiral
center and/or central chirality of the starting allenes, which are
close to those of chiral ligands. Recently, there have been a few
reports on enantioselective 2,3-butadienylation of chiral N-Cu-
metalated azomethine ylides generating optically active 2,3-
butadienyl α-amino acid derivatives using the synergistic Pd/Cu
catalysis with either two different or the same chiral ligands
(Scheme 1a, eq 2).
7
So far, there is no report on the
enantioselective allenylation creating a chiral center on the
nucleophiles by utilizing the chiral palladium catalyst alone
(Scheme 1a, eq 3).
8
The challenge is that the to-be-formed
stereocenter is relatively far from the chiral environment. On the
other hand, oxindoles are prevalent in a wide array of natural
products and bioactive compounds (Scheme 1c)
9
and are also
important synthetic units in organic synthesis.
10
Thus, there is
an urgent need to develop new protocols that provide new
diversified oxindole compounds.
11
Here, we report the first
enantioselective Pd-catalyzed allenylation reaction of oxindoles
with 2,3-allenylic carbonates
12
providing optically active allene
derivatives bearing an oxindole in which an all-carbon
quaternary center was constructed in the 3-position of oxindoles
(Scheme 1b).
Oxindole 1a and 2,3-allenylic tert-butyl carbonate 2a were
selected as the model substrates. Different chiral bidentate
bisphosphine ligand skeletons were screened with Pd(dba)
2
as
the palladium source for the reaction in N,N′-dimethylpropy-
leneurea (DMPU) at −30 °C [Table 1, (R)-L1-(R)-L7]. (R)-L7
was found to be the best ligand and provided the product (R)-
3aa in 50% yield with −39% ee. Then the P-phenyl group of (R)-
L7 was replaced with other substituted phenyl groups [Table 1,
(R)-L8-(R)-L12], and it was found that (R)-L12 with 3,5-(t-
Bu)
2
-4-MeO-phenyl is the best by providing the product (R)-
3aa in 92% yield and 91% ee.
After further optimization, it was observed that when 2.9 mol
% Pd(dba)
2
and 2.9 mol % (R)-DTBM-Biphep [(R)-L12] were
applied, the reaction in DMPU at −30 °C afforded the coupling
product (R)-3aa in the highest yield and enantioselectivity. The
scope of oxindoles was then investigated with 2,3-allenylic tert-
butyl carbonate 2a (Table 2). The R
1
can be aryl groups
substituted with 2-methyl, 2-ethyl, 2-methoxy, 2-isopropyl, 2,4-
dimethyl, 2,5-dimethyl, 4-methoxy-2-methyl, and 4-chloro-2-
methyl groups to afford the products (R)-3aa-(R)-3ha in good
yields and high enantioselectivity (87%−97% yields, 58%−92%
ee, Table 2, entries 1−8). The absolute configuration of the
product was determined by the single-crystal X-ray diffraction
study of (R)-3da (Figure S2). Various substituents (R
2
) on the
aromatic rings were well tolerated. Electron-donating groups
such as p-Me- and p-OMe-containing substrates afforded the

the final product (R)-3oa in 2.2505 g (99% yield and 92% ee,
Table 2, entry 17). However, the enantioselectivity for 3-alkyl-
substituted oxindoles (R)-3ra and (R)-3sa were moderate (63%
and 64% ee) (Table 2, entries 21 and 22).
As a class of highly useful compounds in organic synthesis, the
final product (R)-3oa can be easily transformed to other
multifunctional chemicals with high ee values (Scheme 2): the
N-substituent, tert-butyl carbonate, can be removed to provide
the compound (R)-4 without racemization.
13

15
In conclusion, we have described a general method of the Pd-
catalyzed enantioselective allenylation reaction of oxindoles
with 2,3-allenylic carbonates for the efficient construction of
optically active allene derivatives bearing an oxindole unit. The
reaction works with a wide range of substrates to give the
products in good yield with high enantioselectivity. The
synthetic potentials of the final products have also been
demonstrated. Further studies are being pursued in our
laboratory.
